P2_budget_vs_gpu_busy._claim: the budget must not bind artificially AND its utilisation must track measured GPU busy time (D102, both halves)
P2_budget_vs_gpu_busy.diagnosis: TWO TERMS WERE CHARGED THAT ARE NOT WORK, and each failed a different half. per_queue * queued_ahead is the LATENCY this request SUFFERS because other requests' work is in front of it; charging it bills the same GPU-seconds once per request queued behind them, growing as u^2 k^2 / 2 against linear real work, and it bound the budget artificially on a dry cell (10,612 refusals). The 0.0678 s intercept is per-request OCCUPANCY, not work: it passed the dry half but added 46 and 51 percent of wall clock on the measured cells and took utilisation to 1.07 and 1.34 while the GPU was 60 to 80 percent busy. On the PLANNER side both terms are CORRECT, because there they price the delay a candidate IMPOSES on others
P2_budget_vs_gpu_busy.utilisation_finding: the PER-UNCACHED term tracks measured GPU busy time to 2 percent (737.5 against 721.9 s at s4, 985.3 against 964.5 s at s5), and its implied rate 5,482 tok/s agrees with the committed 5,600 tok/s prefill rate to 2 percent. Its utilisation is 0.61 and 0.82 of wall against measured busy fractions of 0.60 and 0.80, so the charge neither oversubscribes the clock nor undercharges the engine
P2_budget_vs_gpu_busy.gate: refusals at or below 500, plan_state still reaching decisions, the decision log within 10 percent of covex-v6-rules' 4376 rows, the per-uncached term within 10 percent of measured busy time, and no cell oversubscribed
P2_budget_vs_gpu_busy.verdict: PASS: under the ruled uncached-only charge the budget does not bind artificially (0 refusals, 2038 state decisions, 4376 rows against covex-v6-rules' 4376) and its utilisation tracks measured GPU busy time to 2 percent on both committed cells with neither oversubscribed
